ShouldDisappearFromDoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 flags this as the one to think about rather than reflex-waive, so it was traced. EXECUTED: `grep -rn ShouldDisappearFromDoom src/` returns 11 hits -- the virtual at MonsterModel.cs:171, nine monster overrides, and exactly ONE reader, DoomPower.cs:90. That reader sits inside `PlayVfx`, a private static that returns immediately when `NCombatRoom.Instance?.GetCreatureNode(creature)` is null and whose entire body is `StartDoomAnim`, `NDoomOverlayVfx.GetOrCreate()` and two `Cmd.Wait` branches (DoomPower.cs:80-111). The flag chooses an ANIMATION and a wait length; it gates nothing mechanical, and DoomPower's actual kill (`DoomKill`) never reads it. The sim additionally has no DoomPower at all. Presentation.

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's shared verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (the_obscura.py:35-39, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, IllusionPower, 1)`). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:26-40 and relics/paels_legion.py:36-43, and all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, which a self-applied cardless starting power cannot satisfy; (b) HP-roll inversion -- only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:2063, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :1581, logic unchanged); (c) roll ordering -- `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op. Rule 7: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic/potion/power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Escalation check per SHARED-FINDINGS section 2: this unit applies the power to ITSELF (not to the player as Rocket does) and reads nothing from hooks.combat, so none of the escalation conditions apply and the shared verdict fits unchanged.

GenerateMoveStateMachine (protected; add.rationale: THE BATCH'S ONE HAND-ROLLED PORT. C# Parafright.cs:41-48 builds a machine with exactly ONE state -- `MoveState("SLAM_MOVE", SlamMove, SingleAttackIntent(16))` whose FollowUpState is itself -- registered as the only entry and used as the initial state. The reachable state space is therefore a single node with a self-edge: there is no RandomBranchState, no ConditionalBranchState, no AddBranch, no repeat rule and no cooldown (EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py branch-args`: the Parafright half of the_obscura.py has no branch state on either side), so `RollMove` returns SLAM_MOVE on every call for the whole combat and the equivalence proof is an exhaustive enumeration over one state rather than a distribution argument. The sim's `take_turn` (the_obscura.py:54-59) emits exactly that: `_execute_attack(ctx, 16, 1)` every turn, with the one exception below. **The exception is also faithful.** The REVIVE turn is not a machine state in the game either -- IllusionPower.cs:83-88 constructs a synthetic `MoveState("REVIVE_MOVE", ReviveMove, HealIntent())` with `FollowUpStateId = FollowUpStateId ?? StateLog.Last().Id` (= SLAM_MOVE, the only logged state) and hands it to SetMoveImmediate, i.e. one interposed move that then returns to SLAM. The sim reaches the same sequence by short-circuiting take_turn on `illusion.is_reviving` (the_obscura.py:55-58) and telegraphing Intent(MoveType.HEAL) (:50-51). Move sequence on both sides: SLAM* -> REVIVE -> SLAM*. Recorded as deliberate-divergence rather than faithful because the port carries the hand-rolled shape's known costs even though they are inert here: `Monster.telegraph_next_move` is a no-op on the base (monsters/base.py:326, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :96-105, seam step 46), there is no `machine` attribute for FlutterPower's splice (bare filename, was powers.py:2231-2235) and no `_move_key` for CreatureCmd.stun's next-move override (cmds.py:724-743, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :216-217, seam G5) -- none of which any ported caller reaches, because the only ported FlutterPower applier is ThievingHopper and no ported stun targets a Parafright.

ONE MECHANISM ACROSS THIS BATCH (rule 3), recorded at every site: the sim's monster ports drop PowerCmd.Apply's `applier` argument. C# is `Apply<T>(choiceContext, target, amount, applier, cardSource)` (PowerCmd.cs:67) and passes `base.Creature` at Parafright.cs:38 (IllusionPower, applier=base.Creature); the sim's `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target, power_cls, amount, applier=None)` (cmds.py:853-859, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :271-277) is called without it at the_obscura.py:39. In C# a null applier additionally SKIPS the whole Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven pass (PowerCmd.cs:123-126) and changes the key FindExistingInstanceForStacking uses (PowerCmd.cs:78, :112). Same observable today, EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py applier`): the sim has exactly six listener definitions that can see the argument -- powers.py:1172/1181 (ViciousPower, gated `name != "vulnerable" or applier is not self.owner`, powers.py:1167), powers.py:3101/3106 (_PossessPower, gated `applier is self.owner and name == self._stat_id and target.side == "player" and delta < 0`, powers.py:3092-3099), relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 (gated on `target is self.player`, never on applier) and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (gated `applier is not self.player`, unsettling_lamp.py:47). None can distinguish `None` from the applying monster for a power this unit applies. Named trigger: porting any listener that reads `applier` positively (a monster-applier-sensitive relic), or porting PowerInstanceType so stacking is keyed by applier.
